before: When two participants split a paragraph at the same time, and that paragraph came from an earlier concurrent split, the order of the earlier run decided where the new paragraphs showed, and a run inside a moving run was not read. The new paragraphs could show in client ID order, so the text of the original paragraph showed out of order. Tracked break proposals of such a run were placed by the order of the earlier run only. When the split paragraph already proposed its own break, each new paragraph kept a copy of that proposal, and that copy blocked the proposal of the split that ends the paragraph, so rejecting the breaks of one author kept or removed the wrong breaks. A join after such a reject could also put text in the wrong order, because the inline plan counted a moved proposal that two participants listed at once as two blocks.
after: Every concurrent split run is read, also a run inside a run that moves. A nested run orders its paragraphs within the positions that the enclosing run gives them. The paragraph that the nested splits went in before follows them only when the enclosing order shows it after the split paragraph. A nested run that neither split points nor text can order keeps the enclosing order. Each sibling group reads its paragraphs in the order they show, and a break proposal that two groups move shows in one place. When a proposal moves to a sibling that went in right after the same paragraph, and that sibling shows a proposal already, the sibling's proposal is a stale copy of the split paragraph's mark: it shows nowhere, and the moved proposal shows in its place. The inline plan shows a block that two participants listed at once one time, at the first listing, as the materializer does.
reason: The rule changes which order every replica shows for the same shared state, and where tracked break proposals show, so it is repair semantics. A replica with repairVersion 5 can show other paragraph orders and other proposal places for the same state, and local edits on the two would address different paragraphs. repairVersion increases to 6 (format docx-collaboration:1.5.6.1), so the two versions refuse to share a room before any update applies. The rule reads shared state. A local edit that addresses a paragraph, or an element of a moved proposal, lists the proposal where it shows and removes the stale copy it replaces, as it already lists moved proposals, so no stored field or identity changes, and sharedSchemaVersion does not change.
